easy.def: To shake from side to side.
examples: The table will wobble.
My tooth wobbles.
The bike wobbled.

more.def: To move unsteadily from side to side.
examples: The table wobbles when I lean on it.
The bike wobbled when I first learned to ride.
The baby wobbled across the floor.

easy.def: A shaky movement.
examples: The wheel has a wobble.
There was a wobble.
I felt a wobble.

more.def: An unsteady movement from side to side.
examples: The wheel had a wobble that shook the bike.
I felt a wobble in my loose tooth.
A wobble in his voice showed he was nervous.

easy.def: Shaky.
examples: The table is wobbly.
A wobbly tooth.
My legs feel wobbly.

more.def: Shaking from side to side in an unsteady way.
examples: The wobbly table needed a folded paper under one leg.
I have a wobbly tooth that will fall out soon.
My legs felt wobbly after the long run.

easy.def: Great sadness.
examples: The old tale was full of woe.
She cried in woe.
Woe came to the village.

more.def: Deep sadness or trouble, or a big problem.
examples: The story told of the woe of a lost puppy looking for its home.
The farmer's woes began when the rain stopped for a whole summer.
She told us all about her woes with the broken bike.

easy.def: A wild animal like a big dog.
examples: A wolf howled at the moon.
The wolf lives in the forest.
Wolves run in packs.

more.def: A large wild animal that looks like a dog and lives and hunts in a group.
examples: A wolf lifted its head and howled at the moon.
Wolves live in groups called packs.
The gray wolf walked quietly through the snowy woods.

easy.def: A strong, furry animal of cold places.
examples: A wolverine lives in the cold.
The wolverine is strong.
We saw a wolverine.

more.def: A strong, fierce animal of cold northern forests with thick brown fur.
examples: A wolverine roams the cold forests.
The wolverine is small but very strong.
Wolverines have thick fur to keep warm.

easy.def: A female person who is not a child.
examples: The woman waved.
A woman fixed the roof.
That woman is my aunt.

more.def: An adult female person.
examples: The woman at the desk helped us find a book about space.
Many women work as doctors, pilots, and teachers.
She grew up to be a kind and brave woman.

easy.def: An animal from Australia that looks like a small bear and digs holes.
examples: The wombat is from Australia.
A wombat digs holes.
We saw a wombat.

more.def: A short, stocky animal from Australia that has strong claws for digging and lives in burrows.
examples: A wombat dug a hole under the fence.
The wombat has short legs and a round body.
We saw a wombat at the zoo, asleep in its burrow.

easy.def: To think about something and want to know more.
examples: I wonder why the sky is blue.
I wonder what is for lunch.
She wonders where birds sleep.

more.def: To think about something with curiosity, wanting to know the answer.
examples: She wondered how deep the ocean really was.
He wondered if he had locked the door.
I wonder what the world will be like in fifty years.

related.def: A feeling of surprise and wonder.

easy.def: Very, very good.
examples: We had a wonderful day.
The cake smells wonderful.
What a wonderful surprise!

more.def: Very good, in a way that makes you feel happy or amazed.
examples: We had a wonderful time at the beach.
The wonderful smell of fresh bread filled the kitchen.
She sang a wonderful song at the concert.

easy.def: In a very good way.
examples: She sang wonderfully.
The cake tasted wonderfully sweet.
We had a wonderfully fun day.

more.def: In a way that is very good or amazing.
examples: She sang wonderfully at the school concert.
The cake tasted wonderfully sweet and fresh.
The weather was wonderfully warm for our picnic.

easy.def: In a way that shows you are curious.
examples: She looked wonderingly at the stars.
He gazed wonderingly.
The child stared wonderingly.

more.def: In a way that shows you are curious and amazed.
examples: She looked wonderingly at the huge ship.
The child wonderingly touched the soft snow.
He gazed wonderingly at the fireworks.

easy.def: A place full of amazing things.
examples: The snow made a wonderland.
It was a wonderland.
The park was a winter wonderland.

more.def: A place full of beautiful or amazing things.
examples: The snow turned the yard into a winter wonderland.
Alice fell into a strange wonderland.
The toy store was a wonderland for the children.

easy.def: Wonderful and amazing.
examples: It was a wondrous sight.
The cave was wondrous.
She saw wondrous things.

more.def: Causing wonder and delight, as if from a dream.
examples: The children gazed at the wondrous lights.
It was a wondrous sight to see the whales leap.
The explorers found a wondrous cave full of crystals.

easy.def: The hard part of a tree.
examples: The table is made of wood.
We put wood on the fire.
I carved the wood.

more.def: The hard material that trees are made of, used to build things or burn in a fire.
examples: The cabin was built of wood from the nearby forest.
Dad chopped wood for the fire.
A piece of wood floated down the river.

easy.def: A place with many trees.
examples: We walked through the woods.
A fox lives in the woods.
The woods are quiet.

more.def: A large area of land covered with trees, smaller than a forest.
examples: We hiked through the woods and found a stream.
Deer hide in the woods at the edge of town.
The path through the woods was covered in leaves.

easy.def: A person whose job is to cut down trees.
examples: The woodcutter had a big axe.
A woodcutter lived in the woods.
The woodcutter chopped logs.

more.def: A person who cuts down trees or chops wood for a living.
examples: In the fairy tale, a kind woodcutter helped the lost children.
The woodcutter stacked logs beside his cabin.
A woodcutter sharpened his axe before work.

easy.def: Made of wood.
examples: The wooden chair is old.
The toy is wooden.
I sat on a wooden bench.

more.def: Made of wood.
examples: The wooden chair creaked.
She played with a wooden toy train.
A wooden fence ran around the yard.

easy.def: Land covered with trees.
examples: We walked in the woodland.
Deer live in the woodland.
The woodland is quiet.

more.def: Land that is covered with trees.
examples: Deer live in the quiet woodland.
We hiked through the woodland to the lake.
Woodlands are home to owls and foxes.

easy.def: A bird that pecks holes in trees.
examples: A woodpecker tapped the tree.
The woodpecker has a sharp beak.
I heard a woodpecker.

more.def: A bird with a strong, sharp beak that pecks holes in trees to find insects.
examples: A woodpecker tapped on the tree trunk all morning.
The woodpecker drilled a hole to find insects.
Woodpeckers make their nests in holes in trees.

easy.def: A place with many trees.
examples: We walk in the woods.
The woods are quiet.
A fox lives in the woods.

more.def: An area of land covered with trees.
examples: We walked through the woods behind the school.
Deer live in the quiet woods.
A cabin stood deep in the woods.

easy.def: A small building where wood is stored.
examples: The wood is in the woodshed.
The woodshed is small.
We went to the woodshed.

more.def: A small building where firewood is kept.
examples: Dad stacked firewood in the woodshed.
The woodshed was behind the house.
We fetched logs from the woodshed.

easy.def: A man who lives or works in the woods.
examples: The woodsman knew the forest.
A woodsman cut a tree.
The woodsman lived in a cabin.

more.def: A man who lives or works in the woods and knows the forest well.
examples: The woodsman knew every trail in the forest.
A woodsman cut firewood by the cabin.
The old woodsman found the lost child.

easy.def: Things made of wood, like doors and frames.
examples: The woodwork is painted white.
I like the woodwork in this house.
The woodwork is old.

more.def: Parts of a building made of wood, such as doors and trim, or the craft of making things from wood.
examples: The woodwork in the old house was carved by hand.
Dad painted the woodwork around the windows.
I learned woodwork at school and built a birdhouse.

easy.def: Like wood or full of trees.
examples: The path was woody.
A woody smell.
The woody stem is hard.

more.def: Like wood, or covered with trees.
examples: The woody stems of the bush are hard and brown.
We walked through a woody area behind the school.
The candle had a woody smell.

easy.def: The sound a dog makes.
examples: Woof! said the dog.
The puppy said woof.
I heard a loud woof.

more.def: A word for the deep sound a dog makes when it barks.
examples: "Woof!" barked the big dog at the gate.
The puppy answered with a happy woof when she called its name.
Woof, woof! I could hear the dogs next door.

easy.def: The soft, thick hair of a sheep.
examples: Sheep have thick wool.
My hat is made of wool.
The wool keeps me warm.

more.def: The soft, thick hair of sheep, which is spun into yarn and used to make warm clothes and blankets.
examples: Farmers cut the wool off the sheep in the spring.
Grandma knitted a warm scarf from soft blue wool.
Wool socks kept our feet warm on the snowy hike.

easy.def: Made of wool.
examples: A woolen coat.
The woolen hat is warm.
A woolen sock.

more.def: Made of wool.
examples: She wore a woolen scarf in the snow.
The woolen blanket kept us warm.
He knitted woolen socks for winter.

easy.def: Covered with soft hair like wool.
examples: The sheep is woolly.
The woolly mammoth had long hair.
A woolly sweater.

more.def: Covered with or made of wool or soft, curly hair.
examples: The woolly sheep grazed on the hill.
The woolly mammoth lived long ago.
She wore a warm, woolly hat.

easy.def: Dizzy and a little sick.
examples: I felt woozy.
The woozy boy sat.
She was woozy after spinning.

more.def: Feeling dizzy or weak and a little sick.
examples: I felt woozy after spinning in circles.
The woozy boy sat down until it passed.
She was woozy after the long, hot ride.

easy.def: A sound or letters that mean something.
examples: I know that word.
Write a word.
Say the word.

more.def: A sound or a group of letters that has meaning, used when we speak or write.
examples: The word cat has three letters.
She learned a new word in class today.
He could not find the right word to describe it.

easy.def: To do a job or a task.
examples: Dad works at a store.
I work on my homework.
They worked all day.

more.def: To do a job or put effort into a task.
examples: My aunt works at the hospital and helps sick children.
We worked together to clean the park.
The farmer works hard in the fields all summer.

easy.def: To go or run the right way.
examples: The clock works.
My pen does not work.
The plan worked.

more.def: To function properly, or to have the result that was hoped for.
examples: The flashlight does not work because the batteries are dead.
Our plan worked, and we got to the show on time.
This machine works by using the wind.

easy.def: A job or a task.
examples: I have work to do.
Dad goes to work.
This is hard work.

more.def: A job, or effort that is put into doing something.
examples: Building the treehouse was a lot of work.
My mother goes to work at a bakery.
The teacher praised the good work in my notebook.

related.def: Able to work or be done.

easy.def: A person who works too much.
examples: Dad is a workaholic.
A workaholic never rests.
The workaholic worked late.

more.def: A person who works too much and finds it hard to rest.
examples: Dad is such a workaholic that he works on weekends.
A workaholic may forget to play.
The workaholic did not take a vacation.

easy.def: A sturdy table for work.
examples: Dad works at the workbench.
The workbench has tools.
The workbench is wood.

more.def: A strong table where someone makes or fixes things with tools.
examples: Dad built a birdhouse at the workbench.
Tools hung above the workbench.
The workbench was covered in sawdust.

easy.def: A book with questions to work on.
examples: Open your workbook.
The workbook has math.
I wrote in my workbook.

more.def: A book with exercises that students write in as they learn.
examples: Open your math workbook to page ten.
She filled in the pages of her workbook.
The teacher handed out the workbooks.

easy.def: A person who does a job.
examples: The worker fixed the road.
Many workers build houses.
The workers took a break.

more.def: A person who does a job, especially one who works with their hands.
examples: The workers repaired the road.
A factory worker helped make toys.
The bees are hard workers that gather nectar all day.

easy.def: How something works inside.
examples: I saw the workings of the clock.
The workings are small.
We looked at the workings.

more.def: The parts of something and how they work together.
examples: We looked at the inner workings of the clock.
The teacher explained the workings of a pump.
He studied the workings of the machine.

easy.def: The amount of work you have to do.
examples: I have a big workload.
The workload is heavy.
Her workload is light.

more.def: The amount of work that a person or machine has to do.
examples: The teacher has a big workload this week.
A heavy workload kept her busy all night.
Sharing the chores lightens everyone's workload.

easy.def: A man who does work with his hands, like building or fixing.
examples: The workman fixed the roof.
A workman came to the house.
The workman had tools.

more.def: A man whose job is to do physical work such as building or repairing.
examples: The workman climbed the ladder to fix the roof.
A skilled workman built the stone wall.
The workmen wore hard hats.

easy.def: The skill shown in making something.
examples: The workmanship is fine.
I admire the workmanship.
The table shows good workmanship.

more.def: The skill and care shown in making something.
examples: The workmanship on the table is excellent.
I admired the fine workmanship of the chair.
The craftsman's workmanship was carefully done.

easy.def: Exercise that makes your body strong.
examples: We did a workout after school.
I like a morning workout.
The workout made me tired.

more.def: A period of exercise to make your body stronger or to practice a sport.
examples: The team did a hard workout of running and jumping before the game.
Mom goes for a workout at the gym on Tuesday.
A dance class is a fun workout.

easy.def: A place where people work.
examples: The workplace is busy.
My mom's workplace is an office.
We visited a workplace.

more.def: A place where people go to do their jobs, such as an office, a factory or a shop.
examples: My mom's workplace is a big office downtown.
We visited the fire station, and it was a busy workplace.
A safe workplace has rules to protect the workers.

easy.def: A room where you do work.
examples: He works in the workroom.
The workroom has tools.
The workroom is busy.

more.def: A room set aside for work, such as making or fixing things.
examples: Dad fixes bikes in his workroom.
The art workroom had paints and clay.
Tools hung on the walls of the workroom.

easy.def: A paper with questions to work on.
examples: I did a worksheet.
The worksheet is easy.
We got a worksheet.

more.def: A sheet of paper with questions or tasks for students to do.
examples: The teacher handed out a math worksheet.
I finished my spelling worksheet.
The worksheet had ten problems.

easy.def: A room where people build or fix things.
examples: Dad has a workshop in the garage.
The workshop is full of tools.
We built a birdhouse in the workshop.

more.def: A room or building where people make or repair things, or a short class where people learn by doing.
examples: Grandpa keeps his hammers and saws in his workshop behind the house.
We joined a drawing workshop at the library on Saturday.
The workshop taught us how to build and launch a small rocket.

easy.def: The whole Earth and everything on it.
examples: I want to see the world.
The world is big.
Kids all over the world play.

more.def: The planet Earth and all the people, animals, and places on it.
examples: The Amazon is one of the largest rain forests in the world.
People all over the world celebrate the new year.
Our teacher showed us a map of the world.

easy.def: Having to do with life on Earth, not spiritual things.
examples: Worldly goods.
A worldly person.
Worldly things.

more.def: Having to do with life in this world, such as money and things; or having a lot of experience of the world.
examples: The monk gave up his worldly goods and lived simply.
The worldly traveler had visited many countries.
Fame and money are worldly things.

easy.def: All around the world.
examples: It is a worldwide game.
The singer has worldwide fans.
A worldwide club met online.

more.def: Reaching or found in every part of the world.
examples: Soccer is a worldwide sport that people love in almost every country.
The new book became a worldwide success.
Scientists from many countries joined a worldwide search for the rare bird.

easy.def: All around the world.
examples: The song is loved worldwide.
They sell toys worldwide.
People worldwide watched the game.

more.def: In every part of the world.
examples: The movie was shown worldwide in more than fifty languages.
Millions of people worldwide watched the rocket take off.
The company sells its toys worldwide.

easy.def: A small, long, soft animal that lives in the ground.
examples: A worm is in the dirt.
The bird ate a worm.
Worms wiggle.

more.def: A small animal with a long, soft body and no legs that lives in soil.
examples: The robin pulled a worm out of the grass.
Worms make the soil healthy.
After the rain, worms came up on the sidewalk.

easy.def: A small hole that a worm makes.
examples: I saw a wormhole in the apple.
A wormhole was in the wood.
The wormhole was tiny.

more.def: A tunnel made by a worm or insect, or in stories, a shortcut through space.
examples: We found a wormhole in the old apple.
In the science fiction movie, the ship flew through a wormhole to another galaxy.
The old wood had a tiny wormhole in it.

easy.def: Thinking that something bad might happen.
examples: I am worried about my sick cat.
Mom was worried when I was late.
The worried dog waited by the door.

more.def: Feeling uneasy because you think something bad might happen.
examples: He was worried that he would miss the bus.
The farmer is worried about the lack of rain.
She gave me a worried look.

easy.def: In a way that shows you are worried.
examples: She looked worriedly at the sky.
He worriedly checked the door.
The mother glanced worriedly.

more.def: In a way that shows you feel afraid or troubled about something.
examples: She looked worriedly at the dark clouds.
He worriedly checked his pocket for the key.
The mother glanced worriedly at the clock.

easy.def: To feel that something bad may happen.
examples: I worry about the test.
Do not worry.
She worried about her cat.

more.def: To keep thinking in an uneasy way that something bad may happen.
examples: Do not worry, because we have plenty of time.
He worried that he would forget his lines in the play.
My grandmother worries when it snows.

easy.def: A feeling that something bad may happen.
examples: I have a worry.
Her worry went away.
That is no worry.

more.def: An uneasy feeling about something that might go wrong, or the cause of that feeling.
examples: His biggest worry was that he would be late for the bus.
She shared her worry with her teacher, who helped.
Rain is no worry because we have umbrellas.

related.def: A person who worries a lot.

easy.def: Making you feel nervous.
examples: The storm was worrying.
The news was worrying.
A worrying sound came from the car.

more.def: Making you feel afraid or uneasy about something that might happen.
examples: The dark clouds were worrying.
The long silence was worrying.
It was worrying to see the river rise.

easy.def: In a way that makes you worried.
examples: The river rose worryingly.
He was worryingly quiet.
It was worryingly late.

more.def: In a way that causes worry.
examples: The river rose worryingly after the rain.
He was worryingly quiet all day.
The sky grew worryingly dark.

easy.def: To get worse.
examples: The storm may worsen.
The cold worsened.
The weather worsens.

more.def: To become or make something worse.
examples: The storm began to worsen at night.
Her cough worsened, so she saw the doctor.
The traffic worsens at five o'clock.

easy.def: To show love and respect to God.
examples: They worship at the temple.
Many people worship on Sunday.
We worship together.

more.def: To show love and respect for God or a god, often by praying or singing.
examples: Many people worship at church on Sunday.
The family worships together at the temple.
They worshipped in a small chapel.

easy.def: Having a certain price.
examples: The coin is worth a dollar.
The card is worth ten dollars.
The old toy is worth a lot.

more.def: Equal in value to a certain amount of money.
examples: A dime is worth ten cents.
The old stamp is worth fifty dollars.
How much is the painting worth?

easy.def: Good enough to do.
examples: The trip was worth it.
This book is worth reading.
The view is worth the walk.

more.def: Good or useful enough to deserve the time or effort.
examples: The long climb was worth it for the view.
This movie is worth watching again.
Is the museum worth a visit?

easy.def: Having no value.
examples: The broken toy is worthless.
The old paper is worthless.
The coin was worthless.

more.def: Without any value or use.
examples: The broken toy was worthless.
The old coin turned out to be worthless.
A map without names is worthless.

easy.def: Good enough to be worth the time or effort.
examples: Reading is worthwhile.
The trip was worthwhile.
It was a worthwhile walk.

more.def: Important or good enough to be worth the time, money or effort.
examples: Practicing every day is worthwhile when you want to get better.
The long drive was worthwhile because the view was great.
She felt that helping at the shelter was worthwhile.

easy.def: Good enough to deserve something.
examples: She is worthy of the prize.
It is a worthy cause.
He is a worthy winner.

more.def: Deserving respect, praise or attention.
examples: The charity does worthy work.
Helping animals is a worthy cause.
The knight was worthy of the king's trust.

easy.def: A word used to talk about something that may happen.
examples: I would like some milk.
She said she would come.
He would run if he could.

more.def: A word used to talk about something that might happen, or to ask politely.
examples: I would visit the moon if I could ride a rocket.
Would you please pass the salt?
He said he would call us after dinner.

easy.def: An injury where the skin is cut.
examples: The wound was bandaged.
The nurse cleaned the wound.
The wound healed.

more.def: An injury where the skin is cut or broken.
examples: The nurse cleaned and bandaged the wound.
The wound healed in a week.
The soldier's wound was treated.

easy.def: A word for surprise.
examples: Wow, that is big!
Wow, look at the stars!
Wow!

more.def: A word that you say when you are very surprised or impressed.
examples: Wow, that is a huge fish!
Wow, look at all those stars!
Wow, you did it!
